news.title: 🔴 ALERT — Update Firefox & Chrome Now — Exploit Code Is Public
news.excerpt: Mozilla confirmed public exploit code now exists for two critical Firefox flaws (CVE-2026-15718 and CVE-2026-15719); Chrome also shipped emergency fixes for 15 bugs, two critical. Fully close Firefox to install 152.0.6, and in Chrome click Menu → Help → About Google Chrome to force the update now — don't wait for the slow auto-rollout.

news.title: 🔴 ALERT — New "Avalon" Malware Framework Is Spreading Through Phishing Emails
news.excerpt: A dangerous new malware framework named Avalon is spreading through plain-looking phishing emails, packaged with CrownX ransomware. Once opened it can steal passwords, move through your home network, and lock your files for ransom. Never open attachments or click links in unexpected emails — type the web address in yourself.

news.title: 🔴 ALERT — New FTC Text Scam Sends a Fake Photo ID
news.excerpt: Scammers are texting folks pretending to be FTC employees — and they'll send a photo of a fake government badge to look legit. Their pitch: they can recover money you lost in an earlier scam. It's a cruel twist that targets people who've already been burned.

news.title: 🔴 ALERT — 7-Zip Just Patched a Dangerous Flaw — Update Now
news.excerpt: A serious security hole (CVE-2026-14266) was disclosed in 7-Zip, the free file compressor many folks use. Opening a malicious .7z file or a bad webpage could let an attacker run code on your PC — even drop ransomware. The fix is simple: update 7-Zip to version 26.02 (open 7-Zip, click Help, then Check for Updates).

news.title: 🔴 ALERT — CISA Warns: Hackers Are Actively Exploiting On-Prem SharePoint — Patch Now
news.excerpt: CISA added a critical on-prem SharePoint flaw (CVE-2026-56164) to its exploited-vulnerabilities catalog after active attacks. If your org runs SharePoint on its own servers, patch now and rotate machine keys — or pull outside access until you can.

news.title: 🔴 ALERT — New 'CrashStealer' malware hijacks your Mac by faking Apple
news.excerpt: A new macOS infostealer called CrashStealer spreads through fake "Werkbit Setup" sites, impersonating Apple's CrashReporter to steal passwords, browser data, and crypto wallets. If you see "CrashReporter.dmg" in Downloads, don't open it.

posts.headline: Stop fighting codecs — VLC plays any video or audio file free at videolan.org
posts.tip: Download VLC free at videolan.org. It opens every video and music format — MP4, MKV, AVI, FLAC — without hunting for a 'codec pack.' No ads, no popups.
posts.truth: People pay for a media player or Google 'why won't this file play' for an hour. The honest answer is one free app handles all of it, always has, and never pops an ad.

posts.headline: Chat with AI privately in your own browser — Open WebUI is the free local tool at openwebui.com
posts.tip: Install Open WebUI free from openwebui.com (or run 'pip install open-webui') and pair it with Ollama to run AI models on your own PC so your chats never leave the house. No subscription, no cloud.
posts.truth: Folks worry AI is shipping their documents off to some cloud. The honest answer is you can run the exact same models at home — your data never leaves the drive, and there's no monthly fee.

posts.headline: A $35 Raspberry Pi 5 is a real desktop and project computer that fits in your palm
posts.tip: Buy a Raspberry Pi 5 for $35 at raspberrypi.com or Amazon and boot Raspberry Pi OS from a microSD card. It runs a full Linux desktop — perfect for a kid's first PC, a retro game box, or a smart-home hub.
posts.truth: Everyone assumes a 'real computer' costs $600 or more. The honest answer is a $35 board plus the keyboard and TV you already own gets a student online for schoolwork and coding — no Windows tax, no bloat.

posts.headline: Signal is the free messaging app that encrypts every text and call — get it at signal.org
posts.tip: Install Signal free from signal.org or your phone's app store. It's open-source and end-to-end encrypts your texts, calls, and photos so not even Signal can read them.
posts.truth: People tell me 'nobody's reading my texts.' The honest answer is every big messenger scans your messages to sell you ads. Signal literally can't — that's the whole design, and it costs you nothing.

posts.headline: Firefox 152 puts an AI assistant and one-tap site shortcuts in your browser — free at firefox.com
posts.tip: Update free at firefox.com or via the in-app updater (Menu > Help > About Firefox). Firefox 152's new 'Smart Window' summarizes and explains any text you select using a built-in assistant, and the New Tab shows a row of shortcuts back to your favorite sites.
posts.truth: Most people think they're stuck with whatever browser shipped on the machine. The honest answer is you can switch today and keep every password and bookmark — Firefox imports them in two clicks, and it tracks you a whole lot less than the default.

posts.headline: Stop feeding Google your browsing history — Brave is the free browser that blocks trackers by default (brave.com)
posts.tip: Download Brave free from brave.com for Windows, Mac, or Linux. It blocks ads and trackers out of the box — no extensions to install, no settings menus to hunt through.
posts.truth: Most people think "private browsing" in Chrome keeps them private. It doesn't — it only hides your history from the person on your own couch. Brave blocks the trackers that follow you across the entire web, the day you install it, with zero setup.

posts.headline: Encrypt a lost USB stick so it can't expose your tax files — VeraCrypt is the free tool (veracrypt.fr)
posts.tip: Download VeraCrypt free from veracrypt.fr, then create an encrypted container (a locked file) or encrypt a whole USB drive. Your files stay scrambled even if the drive is lost or stolen.
posts.truth: People buy $20 "secure" thumb drives and think they're safe. They're not — a lost drive with plain files is an open book to whoever finds it. VeraCrypt is free, open-source, and has been independently audited. Paying more doesn't make it safer here.

posts.headline: Make AI art and run 100+ AI tools on your own PC free — Pinokio installs them with one click (pinokio.computer)
posts.tip: Get Pinokio free from pinokio.computer for Windows, Mac, or Linux. It's a launcher that installs Stable Diffusion and other AI apps locally with one click — no command line, no Python errors.
posts.truth: Everyone assumes "AI" means a monthly ChatGPT bill and your data sitting in someone else's cloud. Pinokio flips that — it pulls AI models down to your own machine and runs them offline. Free, and nothing leaves the house.
